Q165.L1t: The Taj Mahal is a famous mausoleum in India and one of the best-known monuments in the world.
Q165.L2t: The Taj Mahal was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in childbirth.
Q165.L3t: The passage says workers were brought in from all over India as well as from Central Asia, so the workforce had more than one origin.
Q165.L4t: The statement that every worker came from Central Asia is false, because many workers came from across India too.
Q165.L2f: The Taj Mahal was ordered by Emperor Aurangzeb to honor his mother and was finished within five years.
Q165.L3f: The passage says the Taj Mahal was built from red sandstone, and its colour never changes with the light.
Q165.L4f: The claim that the Taj Mahal was built with white marble stones is the false one.

Q166.L1t: The passage is about the role of school education and the importance of learning beyond the classroom.
Q166.L2t: The writer says a teacher cannot teach students everything, and much must be learned outside school by the students themselves.
Q166.L3t: The writer points out that great scientists like Einstein, Newton and Galileo succeeded because they asked many questions as they read and carried out thousands of experiments.
Q166.L4t: The writer advises us to ask more questions and think more as we study.
Q166.L2f: The writer says Einstein, Newton and Galileo learned everything they knew from their school teachers.
Q166.L3f: The writer says the key to success is to listen closely in class, since teachers can teach students everything they want to know.
Q166.L4f: The writer's advice is that we should pay enough attention to the classroom.

Q167.L1t: The passage discusses how students learn at school and on their own.
Q167.L2t: The writer says it is quite easy to learn a fact or formula, but very difficult to use a formula to work out a maths problem.
Q167.L3t: The writer says knowing how to study by oneself matters more than memorising facts, and that great scientists asked many questions as they read.
Q167.L4t: The most important thing for a student who wants to learn better is to think more while studying.
Q167.L2f: The writer says using a formula to solve a maths problem is easier than memorising the formula.
Q167.L3f: The writer says the teacher's lessons contain everything a student needs, so following the teacher exactly is the way to succeed.
Q167.L4f: The most important thing for a student who wants to learn better is to do everything as the teacher has said in class.
